data.title: New Real-World Evidence Presented by Organon at the American College of Rheumatology (ACR) Annual Meeting Evaluated a Large-Scale Switch to HADLIMA® (adalimumab-bwwd) Across United States Veterans Affairs Healthcare System
data.description:
Organon (), a global healthcare company with a mission to deliver impactful medicines and solutions for a healthier every day, today announced the poster presentation of new real-world evidence at the American College of Rheumatology (ACR) Annual Meeting, held November 6-11, 2026 in Orlando, Florida. The poster evaluates the treatment, management, and economic impacts of transitioning patients from originator HUMIRA® (adalimumab) to biosimilar HADLIMA® (adalimumab-bwwd) within the United States (US) Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Healthcare System.1

The analysis demonstrated that a large-scale health system switch to HADLIMA was achieved with a 1.3% switchback rate over a 12-month follow-up period.1 Though published rates vary, switchback rates from biosimilars to originator are frequently cited as 16-18% in the scientific literature.2,3 Adherence metrics remained similar pre- and post-switch while generating cost savings for the healthcare system, with average per-patient pharmacy costs decreasing by $8,100 in the first year following the switch.1 HADLIMA was exclusively selected by the VA to replace HUMIRA on its national formulary in 2024.4

“The findings demonstrate that a well-managed formulary transition to HADLIMA can deliver both continuity of care and economic savings,” said Jon Martin, US Commercial Lead, Biosimilars and Established Brands at Organon. “Real-world evidence at this scale is critical for showing that biosimilar adoption can support sustainable health systems while delivering confidence to doctors and patients alike. At Organon, we believe in the potential of biosimilars to expand patient access to effective treatments while potentially reducing the affordability burden on health care systems.”

The study analyzed electronic health records and administrative datasets from the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Corporate Data Warehouse, including veterans who received any adalimumab treatment between October 1, 2015, and August 1, 2025, with at least one baseline clinical encounter.1* Patients were categorized into three cohorts: originator HUMIRA only, HADLIMA only, or a switch cohort (transitioning from originator to HADLIMA).

  • Of 58,407 total individuals identified, 16,322 veterans transitioned from the originator to HADLIMA. The switch cohort had a mean age of 60 years and was 87% male and 75% white.1

  • Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) represented the most common diagnosis (21.9%; n= 3577), followed by psoriatic arthritis (PsA; 8.4%; n= 1374), and ankylosing spondylitis (AS; 7.6%; n=1239).1

  • Within 12 months of follow-up, 1.3% of patients switched back from HADLIMA to the originator. Treatment adherence metrics remained similar pre- and post-switch.1

  • Across all indications in the switch cohort, mean per-patient pharmacy costs decreased by $8,100 in the first year following the switch.1

  • At the system level, the switch resulted in $132 million total estimated savings to the Veterans Affairs Healthcare System.1

Poster presentation details

  • Title: Real-World Evidence From the US Veterans Affairs Healthcare System of a Successful Switch to Biosimilar adalimumab-bwwd (Hadlima) from Originator adalimumab (Humira) Following a Formulary Change

  • Presentation date & time: Monday, November 9, 2026, 10:30 AM to 12:30 PM ET

  • Presenter: Ricardo Infante, Medical Affairs Lead, Organon

About HADLIMA® (adalimumab-bwwd) Injection

HADLIMA is a tumor necrosis factor (TNF) blocker indicated for:

  • Rheumatoid Arthritis: HADLIMA is indicated, alone or in combination with methotrexate or other non-biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs), for reducing signs and symptoms, inducing major clinical response, inhibiting the progression of structural damage, and improving physical function in adult patients with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis.

  • Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis: HADLIMA is indicated, alone or in combination with methotrexate, for reducing signs and symptoms of moderately to severely active polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis in patients 2 years of age and older.

  • Psoriatic Arthritis: HADLIMA is indicated, alone or in combination with non-biologic DMARDs, for reducing signs and symptoms, inhibiting the progression of structural damage, and improving physical function in adult patients with active psoriatic arthritis.

  • Ankylosing Spondylitis: HADLIMA is indicated for reducing signs and symptoms in adult patients with active ankylosing spondylitis.

  • Crohn’s Disease: HADLIMA is indicated for the treatment of moderately to severely active Crohn’s disease in adults and pediatric patients 6 years of age and older.

  • Ulcerative Colitis: HADLIMA is indicated for the treatment of moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis in adult patients.

Limitations of Use:

The effectiveness of HADLIMA has not been established in patients who have lost response to or were intolerant to tumor necrosis factor (TNF) blockers.

  • Plaque Psoriasis: HADLIMA is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with moderate to severe chronic plaque psoriasis who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy, and when other systemic therapies are medically less appropriate. HADLIMA should only be administered to patients who will be closely monitored and have regular follow-up visits with a physician.

  • Hidradenitis Suppurativa: HADLIMA is indicated for the treatment of moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa in patients 12 years of age and older.

  • Uveitis: HADLIMA is indicated for the treatment of non-infectious intermediate, posterior, and panuveitis in adult and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older.

SELECTED SAFETY INFORMATION

SERIOUS INFECTIONS
Patients treated with adalimumab products, including HADLIMA, are at increased risk for developing serious infections that may lead to hospitalization or death. Most patients who developed these infections were taking concomitant immunosuppressants such as methotrexate or corticosteroids.

Discontinue HADLIMA if a patient develops a serious infection or sepsis.

Reported infections include:

  • Active tuberculosis (TB), including reactivation of latent TB. Patients with TB have frequently presented with disseminated or extrapulmonary disease. Test patients for latent TB before HADLIMA use and during therapy. Initiate treatment for latent TB prior to HADLIMA use.

  • Invasive fungal infections, including histoplasmosis, coccidioidomycosis, candidiasis, aspergillosis, blastomycosis, and pneumocystosis. Patients with histoplasmosis or other invasive fungal infections may present with disseminated, rather than localized, disease. Antigen and antibody testing for histoplasmosis may be negative in some patients with active infection. Consider empiric anti-fungal therapy in patients at risk for invasive fungal infections who develop severe systemic illness.

  • Bacterial, viral, and other infections due to opportunistic pathogens, including Legionella and Listeria.

Carefully consider the risks and benefits of treatment with HADLIMA prior to initiating therapy in patients:

  • with chronic or recurrent infection

  • who have been exposed to TB

  • with a history of opportunistic infection

  • who resided in or traveled in regions where mycoses are endemic

  • with underlying conditions that may predispose them to infection

Monitor patients closely for the development of signs and symptoms of infection during and after treatment with HADLIMA, including the possible development of TB in patients who tested negative for latent TB infection prior to initiating therapy.

  • Do not start HADLIMA during an active infection, including localized infections.

  • Patients older than 65 years, patients with co-morbid conditions, and/or patients taking concomitant immunosuppressants may be at greater risk of infection.

  • If an infection develops, monitor carefully and initiate appropriate therapy.

  • Drug interactions with biologic products: A higher rate of serious infections has been observed in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients treated with rituximab who received subsequent treatment with a TNF blocker. An increased risk of serious infections has been seen with the combination of TNF blockers with anakinra or abatacept, with no demonstrated added benefit in patients with RA. Concomitant administration of HADLIMA with other biologic DMARDs (eg, anakinra or abatacept) or other TNF blockers is not recommended based on the possible increased risk for infections and other potential pharmacological interactions.

MALIGNANCY

Lymphoma and other malignancies, some fatal, have been reported in children and adolescent patients treated with TNF blockers, including adalimumab products. Postmarketing cases of hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma (HSTCL), a rare type of T-cell lymphoma, have been reported in patients treated with TNF blockers, including adalimumab products. These cases have had a very aggressive disease course and have been fatal. The majority of reported TNF blocker cases have occurred in patients with Crohn’s disease or ulcerative colitis and the majority were in adolescent and young adult males. Almost all of these patients had received treatment with azathioprine or 6-mercaptopurine concomitantly with a TNF blocker at or prior to diagnosis. It is uncertain whether the occurrence of HSTCL is related to use of a TNF blocker or a TNF blocker in combination with these other immunosuppressants.

  • Consider the risks and benefits of HADLIMA treatment prior to initiating or continuing therapy in a patient with known malignancy.

  • In clinical trials, more cases of malignancies were observed among adalimumab-treated subjects compared to control subjects.

  • Non-melanoma skin cancer (NMSC) was reported during clinical trials for adalimumab-treated subjects. Examine all patients, particularly those with a history of prolonged immunosuppressant or psoralen and ultraviolet A (PUVA) therapy, for the presence of NMSC prior to and during treatment with HADLIMA.

  • In adalimumab clinical trials, there was an approximate 3-fold higher rate of lymphoma than expected in the general U.S. population. Patients with chronic inflammatory diseases, particularly those with highly active disease and/or chronic exposure to immunosuppressant therapies, may be at higher risk of lymphoma than the general population, even in the absence of TNF blockers.

  • Postmarketing cases of acute and chronic leukemia were reported with TNF blocker use. Approximately half of the postmarketing cases of malignancies in children, adolescents, and young adults receiving TNF blockers were lymphomas; other cases included rare malignancies associated with immunosuppression and malignancies not usually observed in children and adolescents.

HYPERSENSITIVITY

Anaphylaxis and angioneurotic edema have been reported following adalimumab administration. If a serious allergic reaction occurs, stop HADLIMA and institute appropriate therapy.

HEPATITIS B VIRUS REACTIVATION

Use of TNF blockers, including HADLIMA, may increase the risk of reactivation of hepatitis B virus (HBV) in patients who are chronic carriers. Some cases have been fatal.

Evaluate patients at risk for HBV infection for prior evidence of HBV infection before initiating TNF blocker therapy.

Exercise caution in patients who are carriers of HBV and monitor them during and after HADLIMA treatment.

Discontinue HADLIMA and begin antiviral therapy in patients who develop HBV reactivation. Exercise caution when resuming HADLIMA after HBV treatment.

NEUROLOGIC REACTIONS

TNF blockers, including adalimumab products, have been associated with rare cases of new onset or exacerbation of central nervous system and peripheral demyelinating diseases, including multiple sclerosis, optic neuritis, and Guillain-Barré syndrome.

Exercise caution when considering HADLIMA for patients with these disorders; discontinuation of HADLIMA should be considered if any of these disorders develop.

HEMATOLOGIC REACTIONS

Rare reports of pancytopenia, including aplastic anemia, have been reported with TNF blockers. Medically significant cytopenia has been infrequently reported with adalimumab products.

Consider stopping HADLIMA if significant hematologic abnormalities occur.

CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE

Worsening and new onset congestive heart failure (CHF) has been reported with TNF blockers. Cases of worsening CHF have been observed with adalimumab products; exercise caution and monitor carefully.

AUTOIMMUNITY

Treatment with adalimumab products may result in the formation of autoantibodies and, rarely, in development of a lupus-like syndrome. Discontinue treatment if symptoms of a lupus-like syndrome develop.

IMMUNIZATIONS

Patients on HADLIMA should not receive live vaccines.

Pediatric patients, if possible, should be brought up to date with all immunizations before initiating HADLIMA therapy.

Adalimumab is actively transferred across the placenta during the third trimester of pregnancy and may affect immune response in the in utero-exposed infant. The safety of administering live or live-attenuated vaccines in infants exposed to adalimumab products in utero is unknown. Risks and benefits should be considered prior to vaccinating (live or live-attenuated) exposed infants.

ADVERSE REACTIONS

The most common adverse reactions in adalimumab clinical trials (>10%) were: infections (e.g., upper respiratory, sinusitis), injection site reactions, headache, and rash.

Before prescribing HADLIMA, please read the Prescribing Information, including the Boxed Warning about serious infections and malignancies. The Medication Guide and Instructions for Use also are available.

data.title: J&J's once-daily pill eases psoriatic arthritis symptoms in late-stage trial
data.description:
By Padmanabhan Ananthan

Johnson & Johnson said on Saturday its once-daily pill eased symptoms in more patients with psoriatic arthritis than a placebo in a late-stage trial, potentially supporting expanded use of the drug.

The company said 58% of patients who took icotrokinra, branded as Icotyde, saw a 20% improvement in tender and swollen joint counts, as well as improvements in other measures of disease activity after 16 weeks. That compared with 41% who received a placebo in the 552-patient trial.

Psoriatic arthritis is a long-term inflammatory condition that affects the joints, causing pain, swelling and stiffness.

Icotyde is already FDA-approved for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, a skin condition causing red, scaly, often itchy patches.

The positive results mark another advance for Icotyde, an oral peptide that Wall Street analysts have tipped as J&J's next blockbuster, with potential to take share from established rivals. The company expects peak sales to top $5 billion across multiple indications.

"Patients don't want to be overtreated, they want a treatment that fits them where they're at," David Lee, Johnson & Johnson's global immunology head, told Reuters.

Unlike injectable biologics such as AbbVie's Skyrizi and UCB's Bimzelx, Icotyde is an oral treatment, offering a more convenient option if approved.

Lee added that about 30% of patients with psoriasis also have psoriatic arthritis, highlighting a significant unmet need.

The psoriatic arthritis space is highly competitive, with injectable biologics as well as oral treatments, including Sotyktu and Otezla, already on the market.

The trial enrolled adults with active psoriatic arthritis who had not previously been treated with biologic medicines. The company said no new safety concerns were identified.

Patients taking Icotyde also showed improvements in psoriasis skin symptoms. Among those with sufficient skin involvement, 57% had clear or nearly clear skin after 16 weeks, compared with 14% in placebo, the company said.

data.title: BitFuFu’s October Bitcoin Mining Output Falls Despite Steady Hashrate
data.description:
TL;DR: BitFuFu produced 137 BTC in October, down from 167 in September, while managed hashrate stayed close to 19.5 EH/s. The miner attributed the decline partly to rising network difficulty, illustrating why steady capacity does not necessarily mean steady production.

A Bitcoin miner can run broadly the same amount of computing power and still produce fewer coins. BitFuFu’s latest monthly operating statement provides a neat example. The company reported November 6 that it mined 137 BTC in October, down from 167 in September, even as total hashrate under management remained largely unchanged.

Its managed rate stood at 19.5 exahashes per second, compared with 19.4 EH/s a month earlier. The company held 1,454 BTC at October’s end, up from 1,388 in September. Production decreased while the treasury balance increased, because production and coin retention are separate measures.

Difficulty makes the same equipment earn less

BitFuFu said Bitcoin network difficulty rose about 11.8% during October, from 132.76 trillion at the beginning of the month to 148.36 trillion at month-end. Difficulty adjusts how hard it is for miners collectively to find valid blocks. When competition increases, a miner with an unchanged share of computing power may capture a smaller share of the rewards than before.

The split inside BitFuFu’s operation was also revealing. Self-mining production fell to 67 BTC from 98 BTC, while cloud-mining production was nearly flat at 70 BTC against 69 BTC in September. Total monthly production therefore declined by 30 BTC, but the effect was not identical across its operating categories.

NewsBTC recently examined Bitcoin’s recovery above one zettahash of network hashrate. That broader competition can be healthy for network security while making mining economics more demanding for individual operators. It is possible for both statements to be true at once.

Efficiency improves, but economics remain demanding

BitFuFu’s average fleet efficiency improved to 16.3 joules per terahash from 16.7 in September. Lower energy use per unit of hashing is useful, although it does not automatically offset higher difficulty, power prices, financing costs or changes in Bitcoin’s market price. The company also reported power capacity under management of 317 megawatts, compared with 324 MW a month earlier.

These figures are particularly relevant when evaluating mining businesses that sell both direct Bitcoin exposure and computing services. Managed hashrate can include machines owned by clients or supplied by third parties, not just equipment on the company’s balance sheet. Investors should therefore distinguish self-owned hashrate, contractual capacity, energy efficiency and coins actually received.

A miner accumulating coins can improve its Bitcoin exposure even while production slows. But treasury growth alone says little about the cost of producing each BTC or the cash needed to keep equipment operating. The real test is whether operations remain resilient when difficulty rises and the market price fails to keep pace.

What November’s update should establish

The next report will show whether October’s production weakness was temporary or persisted under the next difficulty environment. Useful metrics include self-mined output, third-party mining contribution, installed and energised capacity, average fleet efficiency and the amount of Bitcoin retained rather than sold.

BitFuFu’s figures are unaudited operating metrics, not a full measure of profitability. They nevertheless make the central point clearly: Bitcoin mining is a competitive process, and an operator can improve its hardware efficiency while producing fewer coins. That is why mining comparisons need more than a headline hashrate number.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: 5 out of 6 communications services stocks deliver EPS wins this week: Earnings Scorecard
data.description:
Communications services stocks grabbed the spotlight this week as Wall Street digested earnings reports from major names, including Charter Communications and Fox .

The communications services sector lost over 11% so far this year, compared to the 7% rise in the broader S&P 500 Index.

In this week's earnings recap, six tickers reported results, five (83%) of which reported earnings beats. On the revenue side, five companies exceeded revenue expectations, while one company trailed estimates.

Below are the latest quarterly reports from some key players, which reported results this week:

Shares of Fox closed over 6% higher on Tuesday after the media company reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 results that topped estimates, as the FIFA Men's World Cup, political advertising, and digital growth lifted revenue. Revenue for the quarter increased 22% to $4.57 billion, beating the $4.32 billion consensus estimate, while adjusted EPS was $2.54, above the $2.01 estimate.

Charter Communications , meanwhile, reported wider internet customer losses in the third quarter, underscoring the pressure on its broadband business even as it laid out a new operating model aimed at returning to customer growth and cutting costs. The company lost 233,000 internet customers on a pro forma basis in the quarter, compared with a decline of 171,000 a year earlier. Revenue rose 9.1% to $14.92 billion, exceeding the $13.74 billion consensus estimate, while adjusted EBITDA increased 6.9% to $5.94 billion, above the $5.86 billion estimate.

AppLovin shares surged after the advertising technology company reported third-quarter results that topped Bloomberg estimates and issued fourth-quarter guidance above expectations. The company posted revenue of $2.18 billion, up 55% year-over-year, beating the Bloomberg consensus estimate of $2.07 billion. Diluted EPS came in at $4.30, compared with expectations of $4.04.

For the upcoming week, Take Two Interactive Software is one important communication services name that is scheduled to report quarterly results.

data.title: Berkshire Hathaway, Mastercard, Visa among gainers; Goldman Sachs in losers: week's financials wrap
data.description:
Wall Street's major indexes went from cheerful optimism after the 2026 midterm elections to experiencing their worst day in over a year and a half. All three major indexes saw severe week-to-date losses from an ongoing technology selloff and policy fears related to AI.

However, the State Street Financial Sel Sec SPDR ETF added 1.15% week-over-week to close at $57.16.

United States 10-Year Bond Yield slid to 4.87% from 4.93% during the course of the week. Lower long-term rates help banks by lowering the impact of accumulated other comprehensive income on deal marks, S&P Global Market Intelligence reported, citing an interview with StoneX Managing Director Brett Rabatin.

Meanwhile, insurance indexes remained in positive territory for the week.

Among megacap financial stocks, Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B) (BRK.A) led the gainers, advancing 5.24% and 5.03% from the previous week to close at $570.89 and $856,612.00, respectively.

The stock was rising ahead of the company's scheduled Q3 earnings announcement. For the third quarter, the investing behemoth reported operating earnings of $12.7B (-5.8% Y/Y).

Mastercard and Visa followed, adding 2.30% and 2.19% to $652.70 and $422.65, respectively.

With Democrats winning the midterm elections, the ideas President Trump endorsed, such as capping credit card interest at 10%, face stronger opposition. Credit card stocks stand to benefit.

Goldman Sachs Group (-3.21% W/W to $865.82) and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial (-2.74% W/W to $20.97) led the weekly losers in the category.

Bank stocks fell but outperformed broader markets during the week, the worst week of the year for the market, according to a report by S&P Global Market Intelligence.

The stock market rise in the morning after the election was partly a "relief rally" after a period of uncertainty. However, a reversal into negative territory reflected investors' belief that the war with Iran may last longer than expected, Stifel Chief Washington Policy Analyst Brian Gardner reportedly said.

Truist Securities analysts reportedly said that they were "surprised that banks outperformed (albeit modestly) on the strong Blue Wave this week." The favorable regulatory backdrop for banks will last for at least two more years, but control of Congress does not actually move the needle for banks.

Life and health insurers Unum Group (-15.79% W/W to $76.75) and Sun Life Financial (-11.59% W/W to $71.53) led the largecap losers. The stocks lost out on the back of their quarterly results announcement.

Rocket Companies (+17.66% W/W to $15.06) led the gainers in the category. Democratic sweep gave a boost to most housing-related stocks.

Among midcap stocks, Riot Platforms (+30.44% W/W to $16.71) was the top winner. The stock jumped as the crypto miner and data center operator reported third-quarter earnings above analyst estimates and its largest lease in history.

Ethos Technologies (-22.77% W/W to $33.51) topped the losers as the tech rout spread into insurtech. The Nasdaq Composite suffered its steepest one-day decline in 19 months on Thursday, confirming a correction and ending in a fourth consecutive weekly loss.

Another stock endorsed by the Trump administration and a crypto treasury firm, Hyperliquid Strategies (-19.94% W/W to $8.82), was the next major loser in the category. Additionally, the week saw the company report its first-quarter fiscal earnings.

PRA Group (-33.71% W/W to $12.92), Evernorth (-25.49% W/W to $10.58), and LendingTree (+32.46% W/W to $37.01) were the notable smallcap movers.

data.title: IHCL opens Himalayan Woodcroft, Sirmaur – IHCL SeleQtions in Himachal Pradesh
data.description:
The Indian Hotels Company (IHCL) has announced the opening of Himalayan Woodcroft, Sirmaur – IHCL SeleQtions in Himachal Pradesh, expanding its leisure portfolio in the state.

Commenting on the opening, Gaurav Pokhariyal, Chief Operating Officer, Full-Service Business, IHCL, said, “As travellers increasingly seek experiences rooted in destination and local character, demand for leisure offerings in emerging markets continues to grow. SeleQtions celebrates hotels with a strong sense of place and individual character. Himalayan Woodcroft, Sirmaur – IHCL SeleQtions reflects this ethos and strengthens our presence in Himachal Pradesh’s leisure travel circuit.”

Nestled in the Himalayan highlands, the 41-key property draws inspiration from the region’s architectural heritage and is built in the traditional Kathkuni style using locally sourced stone and deodar wood. Spread across six acres and surrounded by pine and banj oak forests, the hotel offers views of the valley and the snow-capped Churdhar peak. Designed as a hillside hamlet, it features independent cottages with wooden interiors, valley-facing windows and private sit-outs.

Bijayan Sinha, Hotel Manager, Himalayan Woodcroft, Sirmaur – IHCL SeleQtions, said, “Himalayan Woodcroft offers guests an opportunity to experience the natural beauty and tranquillity of Sirmaur in a setting inspired by the region’s architectural heritage. We look forward to welcoming travellers to this hillside escape.”

The hotel’s dining options include Woodcroft Nest, an all-day restaurant serving Indian, regional and international cuisine, and Mist, a bar overlooking the valley. Facilities also include a swimming pool set along the hillside and a fitness centre.

data.title: Lemon Tree Hotels signs Keys Select property in Mathura
data.description:
Lemon Tree Hotels Limited has announced the signing of Keys Select by Lemon Tree Hotels, Mathura. The property will be managed by Carnation Hotels Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of Lemon Tree Hotels Limited, marking the group’s entry into the city and further strengthening its presence in Uttar Pradesh.

Mathura is a religious and cultural destination that attracts visitors throughout the year for its spiritual heritage and historical significance. Its location within the Agra–Mathura–Vrindavan tourism belt makes it an important market for hospitality development, catering to leisure and business travellers.

The upcoming hotel will feature 65 rooms, along with a restaurant, banquet hall, meeting and conference facilities, swimming pool, spa, fitness centre and other public areas.

Commenting on the signing, Vishvapreet Singh Cheema, President, Lemon Tree Hotels Ltd., said, “Uttar Pradesh is an important market for us, with strong demand across religious tourism, leisure and business travel. The Agra–Mathura–Vrindavan trail, in particular, attracts visitors throughout the year. With an operational Lemon Tree Hotel in Agra and Keys Select by Lemon Tree Hotels, Vrindavan in the pipeline, the Mathura signing further builds our presence across this important pilgrimage and leisure destination. Together, these properties will enhance our ability to serve travellers to the region, offering comfortable stays and warm, consistent hospitality that makes Lemon Tree Hotels a preferred choice.”

data.title: Coca-Cola India's Bottling Arm HCCH Files DRHP For IPO
data.description:
Coca-Cola's holding company for its Indian bottling business has filed IPO papers with Sebi, with promoter Hindustan Coca-Cola Overseas Holdings proposing to offload up to 99.75 crore shares through an offer for sale.

Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings (HCCH), the holding company of Coca-Cola's Indian bottling operations, has filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) for an initial public offering (IPO) comprising an offer for sale of up to 99.75 crore equity shares.

The proposed IPO will see promoter Hindustan Coca-Cola Overseas Holdings Pte Ltd sell up to 99.75 crore shares, each with a face value of Rs 10. The issue will comprise entirely an offer for sale, meaning HCCH will not receive any proceeds from the transaction, with the entire amount going to the selling shareholder.

The proposed share sale marks a step in Coca-Cola's broader strategy to reduce its direct exposure to bottling operations globally and move towards an asset-light, franchise-led business model.

Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages is among Coca-Cola's largest bottling partners in India, manufacturing, packaging and distributing beverages across the country.

Hindustan Coca-Cola Overseas Holdings currently owns 60 per cent of HCCH's equity share capital, while Jubilant Beverages Ltd holds the remaining 40 per cent. Jubilant Beverages became a promoter of HCCH in July 2025.

HCCH's portfolio includes some of Coca-Cola's leading beverage brands in India, such as Coca-Cola, Thums Up, Sprite, Fanta, Limca, Monster, Schweppes, Kinley, Maaza and Minute Maid.

The IPO's book-running lead managers are Kotak Investment Banking, Citi Global Markets India, J.P. Morgan India, Morgan Stanley India, Axis Capital, Goldman Sachs India and IIFL Capital Services.

data.title: Tata Steel beats Q2 profit estimates on strong demand, cost savings
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- Tata Steel Ltd's net profit beat Street estimates in the September quarter (Q2FY27), aided by strong demand and cost-saving measures.

The Mumbai-headquartered steelmaker reported an 18% year-on-year (y-o-y) increase in consolidated net profit to Rs.3,666.41 crore in Q2FY27, according to an exchange filing on Saturday. The company beat Bloomberg's consensus estimate of Rs.3,253.7 crore based on a poll of 12 analysts.

The company also announced that Noel Naval Tata will retire as the non-executive, non-independent director and vice chairman of the board, effective close of business hours on 11 November. It is yet to announce a new vice chairman.

India's second largest steelmaker by capacity delivered cost savings of only Rs.1,800 crore in the first half of FY27, against its full-year target of Rs.7,000 crore, as disruptions across its operations delayed the benefits of its cost-cutting programme.

"The crisis in West Asia, the planned shutdown in India, the direct sheet mill outage in the Netherlands and the unfortunate fire in Tata Steel UK has distorted some of the cost takeout profile. As a result, the benefits of our cost transformation were not fully visible on the reported numbers," executive director and chief financial officer Koushik Chatterjee said during the company's September-quarter earnings call on Saturday. However, Chatterjee said that the guidance remains unchanged and that "the program is generally weighed on the second half."

Tata Steel had delivered cost savings of around Rs.11,000 crore last financial year.

Consolidated revenue from operations rose 12% y-o-y to Rs.65,436.24 crore, while earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization (Ebitda) increased 17% to Rs.10,665 crore. Tata Steel's domestic crude steel production and sales rose to 6.18 million tonnes and 5.98 mt, respectively, from 5.64 mt and 5.55 mt.

"Combination of industry tailwinds, company-specific cost initiatives, and iron ore monetisation led to strong earnings," said Ritesh Shah, joint head of research, analyst - materials, Investec India.

The performance of Tata Steel's European operations remained uneven. In the Netherlands, the restart of the Direct Sheet Plant (DSP) in August helped improve operational performance and product mix. The facility, with an annual processing capacity of around 1.4 million tonnes, had remained shut for most of the first quarter because of regulatory issues.

The Netherlands business reported a revenue of €2,840 million in September quarter, up from €1,551 million in the same quarter last year and an Ebitda of €72 million against €92 million.

However, its long-term outlook remains dependent on regulatory clarity and the economics of its proposed decarbonisation transition. Tata Steel, the Dutch government and the Province of North Holland have extended their joint letter of intent by five months to March 2027 to resolve issues concerning the proposed closure of coke and gas plants, steel slag management, energy affordability and the investment framework.

The UK business, meanwhile, continues to face weak demand and elevated imports. Sales stood at around 400,000 tonnes in the September quarter, below the company's desired level of 500,000-600,000 tonnes a quarter. Steel inventories in the UK had climbed to around 865,000 tonnes by September, nearly 60% above normal levels, following a surge in imports and an exception from quotas for orders booked before 14 March 2026. UK's exports to the EU are now subject to restrictions creating a further constraint on market access, Narendran said.

Although UK steel prices and spreads have improved, lower volumes are hurting profitability because of the business's high fixed-cost base. Tata Steel has already removed nearly £400 million in fixed costs from the UK operations. In the UK, Ebitda loss narrowed to £57 million from £66 million in Q2FY26.

"The prices are good, the spreads are good, but the volumes are not good," Narendran said, adding that the company expects the UK business to approach breakeven in the March quarter as excess inventories gradually clear.

The UK still remains a work in progress with break- even remaining elusive, said the Investec analyst. Even for the electric arc furnace, we await clarity on its cost curve positioning, which will determine its profitability, said Shah.

The steelmaker is replacing its blast furnaces with an electric arc furnace (EAF) at Port Talbot under an agreement with the UK government with the commissioning of the EAF project to be starting in FY29.

Going forward, Tata Steel expects improved steel realisations across geographies in the December quarter. In India, realisations are expected to increase by Rs.3,500-3,600 per tonne sequentially.

Coking coal costs are expected to increase by around $15 per tonne in India and the Netherlands in the December quarter compared with the September quarter. The Netherlands is expected to benefit from a $5-per-tonne reduction in iron ore consumption costs.

Management expects the second half of FY27 to be stronger than the first, supported by higher volumes, improved realisations and seasonally stronger demand.

data.title: Trial failures of Novartis, Novo Nordisk heart drugs leave experts guessing
data.description:
Key points:
  • Pelacarsen cuts Lp(a) 78% but fails to prevent recurrent cardiovascular events in trial of more than 8,300 patients
  • About 20% of global population has high Lp(a), and no approved treatments exist
  • Novo's ziltivekimab lowers inflammation but misses goal in 6,300-patient heart disease trial

By Julie Steenhuysen

An experimental Novartis drug designed to treat a genetic cause of heart disease failed to reduce deaths and non-fatal heart attacks, dashing hopes for the first of several such drugs in clinical trials.

Despite a 78% reduction of the blood particle commonly known as Lp(a), a monthly dose of the Novartis drug, pelacarsen, over nearly five years had no effect in preventing a second heart attack, or reducing the risk of stroke or need for emergency procedures to unblock clogged arteries in the trial of more than 8,300 patients, according to detailed results.

"Everybody in the world, me included, thought that this was going to work," said Dr. Steven Nissen of the Cleveland Clinic, who presented the results on Saturday at the American Heart Association meeting in Chicago.

In September, Novartis and co-developer Ionis Pharmaceuticals announced that their drug had failed to meet the trial's main goal, but experts and investors were eager for details to see if the treatment had some benefit.

"It didn't do anything. It was completely neutral," Nissen said in an interview.

A second failed study testing a Novo Nordisk drug aimed at reducing heart inflammation presented at the AHA meeting likewise hit the intended target of reducing inflammation, but failed to prevent major adverse cardiovascular events.

Taken together, the findings question some foundational theories about key factors underpinning heart disease.

Currently, there are no treatments for patients with high Lp(a), a genetic risk factor for heart disease estimated to affect roughly 20% of the global population, though few individuals know they have it.

Researchers were hoping lowering Lp(a) would yield similar benefits to drugs like statins that significantly reduce the risk of heart attacks and strokes by knocking down levels of LDL, the so-called bad cholesterol.

STUDY DETAILS AND ANALYSIS

Patients were randomized to a monthly 70-milligram dose of pelacarsen or a placebo and followed for a median of 4.7 years.

All patients had a previous major cardiovascular event, such as a heart attack. Other risk factors like high LDL cholesterol and blood pressure were carefully controlled.

Nevertheless, the drug failed to provide any meaningful benefits.

Some 20.6% of patients stopped taking pelacarsen due to adverse effects versus 7.5% among those who received a placebo.

In addition to the study presented on Saturday and published in the New England Journal of Medicine, the team did a separate statistical analysis published in NEJM Evidence. The analysis looked across several measures, including patients who had a higher-than-average reduction in Lp(a) after three months, and only looking at patients who remained in the trial, and it still showed no benefit.

Dr. Donald Lloyd-Jones, a professor of cardiology at Boston University, said in a media briefing that he would not recommend abandoning Lp(a) as a causal risk factor or as a therapeutic target until there is a lot more data in different patient populations.

Pelacarsen belongs to a class of drugs called antisense oligonucleotides, or ASOs, that reduce the production of proteins made by faulty genes.

Other experimental drugs targeting Lp(a), such as Amgen's olpasiran and Eli Lilly's lepodisiran, rely on small interfering RNA, or siRNA, and have been shown to lower Lp(a) levels by around 95%.

Nissen, who is also leading the lepodisiran trial, said there is still strong evidence that Lp(a) is a major cause of heart disease, and suggested differences between pelacarsen and other treatments that may sway the outcome of future trials.

He noted that pelacarsen was tested in people who had already had one major cardiovascular event, while the trials being run by Lilly and Amgen include more patients who have never had a heart attack or stroke.

He also said that siRNAs have been shown to be better tolerated and have higher efficacy. "Whether that will translate into better outcomes remains to be seen."

Amgen's Phase 3 results are expected in early 2028, while Lilly's are expected in 2029.

TOO LATE TO TREAT?

Dr. Paul Ridker of Harvard's Brigham and Women's Hospital, a pioneer in explaining the link between inflammation and heart disease, on Saturday presented trial results for Novo Nordisk's ziltivekimab, an anti-inflammatory drug designed to neutralize interleukin-6, a key source of inflammation in high-risk heart patients.

The Danish drugmaker, best known for its GLP-1 diabetes and obesity drugs, in July announced that the study, which involved 6,300 patients with heart disease, advanced kidney disease and systemic inflammation, failed to show a benefit.

Although the drug lowered inflammation as intended, it did not translate into reduced risk of death, heart attacks or strokes compared with a placebo.

The news shocked many experts and dimmed Novo's hopes of expanding beyond its blockbuster GLP-1 franchises.

On September 7, Novo ended two other late-stage trials evaluating ziltivekimab in patients with heart failure and inflammation based on the recommendation of an independent data monitoring committee, which concluded the trials were unlikely to succeed.

Ridker raised the possibility that the drug was studied in a population whose disease was too advanced to respond to anti-inflammatory intervention, but said targeting inflammation remains compelling.

Dr. Priscilla Hsue of UCLA, who was not involved in the study, said at the briefing that the ziltivekimab trial involved an incredibly sick population and it was possible that inflammation had already done its harm.

Given similarly disappointing outcomes for these two drugs, Lloyd-Jones said, "It's clear we need further trials using different compounds and different strategies."

data.title: 'We're losing to cottage cheese': The protein-maxxing craze is hurting cream-cheese sales
data.description:
By Bill Peters

U.S. sales of cottage cheese have more than doubled from levels seen in 2021

Cottage cheese is making a comeback thanks to social-media videos and a protein craze.

After spending years forsaken in Americans' refrigerators, cottage cheese is staging a comeback, and that is weighing on sales of cream cheese.

Kraft-Heinz said Wednesday that as the ongoing protein craze drives more people to buy cottage cheese, its Philadelphia Cream Cheese brand - which commands a majority of the U.S. market for cream cheese - was falling behind.

"What Philly needs from a category perspective is more innovation, because it's very clear where we're losing as a category," CEO Steve Cahillane said on Kraft Heinz's (KHC) post-earnings-report conference call. "We're losing to cottage cheese and other more protein-forward [items]."

"We need to do more innovation around what the consumer is looking for, vis-à-vis protein, vis-à-vis flavors, vis-à-vis overall innovation," he added.

U.S. cottage-cheese sales rose 17.7% to around $2.32 billion for the 52-week period that ended Oct. 4, more than double the level seen in 2021, data from Circana show. By contrast, sales of cream cheese over that period fell 4.4% to around $2.88 billion.

For years, cottage cheese was more tolerated as a healthy choice than it was actually enjoyed. But in recent years, producers haven't been able make enough of it. Now the cheese is being used as a spread and appearing in recipes for everything from scrambled eggs to ice cream. The food industry is taking notice.

Analysts credit "protein-maxxing" - the social-media-driven protein craze - as a factor behind the surge in demand. Use of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs has also played a role, as people look for ways to get more nutrients into their diet.

"It's perceived as a high-protein way to keep your muscle mass up when you're on GLP-1s," said Brian Walton, an economist at Bozic, a dairy-market data tracker.

Melissa Altobelli, a dairy analyst at Circana, said the resurrection of cottage cheese started a few years ago after the diary product went viral on TikTok, with people watching cooking videos to get ideas for how to use it, she said.

A shift away from larger meals and toward snacking has benefited products like cottage cheese and yogurt, given their nutritional value and the way they're often packaged, which can make them easier to eat on the go.

"More than half of consumers report snacking three or more times per day, and snacking occasions are increasingly replacing traditional meals rather than simply occurring between them," Altobelli said.

The protein boom has led to tighter supplies of whey, a high-protein dairy byproduct often found in drinks and snacks, driving up prices. According to government data, the price of Class II milk - used to make cottage cheese and other soft dairy products - stood at $19.15 per hundredweight, or 100 pounds, in October. That was off higher levels reached at various points earlier this decade, according to a compilation of those prices provided by Bozic. However, costs for other products beyond cottage cheese also influence those prices.

Production levels for cottage cheese are still lower than during the boom seen in the 1970s, which eventually gave way to yogurt. But some large companies are spending more on production.

Carl Colizza, CEO of dairy processor Saputo (CA:SAP) - one of the biggest makers of cottage cheese in North America - said in September that it was trying to keep pace with consumers' appetites. During a conference that month, he cited "a couple of exciting areas where we're investing in additional capacity, like in cottage cheese and in some cultured products where we are struggling to meet demand."

Cottage cheese is attracting investments of other kinds. In January, investment firm L Catterton said it would take a majority stake in the dairy brand Good Culture. In a release, L Catterton said Good Culture's sales had increased nearly fourfold over the prior three years.

"In 2014, I realized there was massive whitespace in a stale category that was lacking innovation," Jesse Merrill, Good Culture's co-founder and CEO, said in that release.

As for cream cheese, Kraft Heinz in September said it would roll out new versions of Philadelphia Cream Cheese, with flavors like hot honey, cranberry orange and salted caramel, in an effort to stand out on grocery shelves. The company also recently launched a lactose-free cream cheese under the Philadelphia name. The Philadelphia brand had roughly 62% of the market share for U.S. for spreadable cheese last year, according to Euromonitor International.

Kraft Heinz's sales fell 2% in the third quarter as the consumer-goods industry coped with shopper caution and stiffer competition. But on Wednesday's call, Cahillane downplayed the threat to cream cheese posed by cottage cheese's ascent.

"There's nothing wrong with the brand," he said of the company's Philadelphia line. "It's just the category is under some pressure relative to switching out of cream cheese into cottage cheese and others. And that's very addressable, but it's going to take just a little bit of time."

-Bill Peters

data.title: Air pollution in India: Does health insurance cover pollution-related illnesses? What policyholders should know
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- With Diwali celebrations bringing families together, health protection deserves as much attention as festive shopping and financial planning. For people living in cities that regularly experience poor air quality, respiratory illnesses such as asthma, bronchitis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and respiratory infections can be a particular concern, especially as pollution levels rise during the winter months.

While health insurance can help cover the financial burden of hospitalisation due to respiratory complications, policyholders should not assume that every pollution-related medical expense will be reimbursed.

Shrish Mahuli, Chief Business Officer at SBI General Insurance, said claims arising from respiratory conditions are assessed based on the nature of the illness, the insured person's medical history and the applicable policy provisions. Policyholders should check waiting periods, exclusions and other conditions to understand the extent of their coverage.

Generally, health insurance policies cover medically necessary hospitalisation for respiratory conditions such as asthma, bronchitis, COPD and respiratory infections, subject to policy terms and conditions.

However, coverage is primarily for eligible hospitalisation expenses and does not necessarily extend to routine outpatient treatment. Doctor consultations, inhalers, over-the-counter medicines and nebulisers used at home are generally not covered unless the policy offers outpatient department (OPD) benefits.

Vineet Gupta, Head of Product Development at ManipalCigna Health Insurance, said coverage is determined by the medical condition and the need for hospitalisation rather than whether pollution caused or aggravated the illness.

Ajay Shah, MD and CEO of Care Health Insurance, said eligible in-patient hospitalisation expenses can include room rent, ICU charges, doctors' fees, medicines, diagnostic tests, ambulance services and pre- and post-hospitalisation expenses, subject to the policy's limits.

This is particularly important for individuals who already have asthma, COPD or other respiratory conditions.

If air pollution aggravates an existing condition, the claim may be treated as a claim relating to a pre-existing disease. In such cases, the policyholder must have completed the applicable waiting period for the treatment expenses to become eligible.

Gupta said most health insurance policies have a PED waiting period of 36 months, although the duration varies across products. Some insurers allow customers to reduce this period by paying an additional premium. Certain policies may also offer coverage for declared and accepted pre-existing conditions from day one.

Policyholders should disclose existing respiratory conditions, previous diagnoses and regular medication at the time of purchasing health insurance. Non-disclosure can create complications when filing claims.

Severe respiratory complications can sometimes require emergency hospitalisation, oxygen support or intensive care. Health insurance can provide financial protection against these expenses when the treatment meets the policy's conditions.

Gupta said hospitalisation involving oxygen support and ICU treatment is covered under standard health insurance policies when medically necessary. However, the hospitalisation must meet the minimum continuous hospital stay requirement specified in the policy.

Mahuli said the admissibility of such claims depends on medical necessity, the treating doctor's recommendations and the applicable policy provisions. Policyholders should also check ICU coverage, room rent limits and the sum insured to understand their financial protection.

With respiratory illnesses potentially affecting multiple family members, choosing an adequate sum insured becomes important.

Shah said families living in cities with persistently poor air quality should consider policies with automatic restoration benefits. These allow the sum insured to be replenished after it is exhausted, subject to policy conditions, helping cover subsequent hospitalisations.

A super top-up policy can also increase the overall health cover at a relatively lower premium. However, consumers should check its deductible and other conditions before buying one.

A policy with a high sum insured may still leave policyholders with substantial out-of-pocket expenses if it has restrictive conditions. Room rent caps, ICU limits, co-payment clauses and disease-specific sub-limits can reduce the amount an insurer pays towards a hospital bill.

Shah recommends checking for policies without room rent or ICU capping and disease-wise sub-limits. Such restrictions can affect the final claim settlement and, in some cases, result in proportionate deductions.

Mahuli also advises consumers to examine ambulance cover and pre- and post-hospitalisation benefits when comparing policies.

Not every pollution-related health problem requires hospitalisation. Many respiratory conditions are managed through regular doctor consultations, diagnostic tests, lung-function assessments and medication.

Standard health insurance policies generally do not cover these routine expenses unless they include OPD benefits.

Gupta recommends checking whether a policy offers OPD or chronic-care add-ons that can help meet expenses such as consultations, diagnostics and inhalers. A wide cashless hospital network and e-consultation facilities can also be useful.

Shah highlighted the importance of understanding which family members are most vulnerable to respiratory illnesses.

According to Care Health Insurance's claims data, children aged 0-12 accounted for 40% of its respiratory hospitalisation claims in FY26, while senior citizens aged 60 and above accounted for 17%. Together, these age groups contributed 58% of such claims during the year.

Ultimately, consumers should look beyond the headline sum insured when buying health insurance. Waiting periods, exclusions, hospitalisation benefits, restoration features and coverage for routine medical expenses all determine how useful a policy can be when a family member needs treatment.

For families living in cities with poor air quality, reviewing these details before the winter pollution season sets in can help avoid unpleasant surprises at the time of a claim.

data.title: Trending stocks this week as Wall Street ends sharply lower
data.description:
The U.S. stock market was marked this week by a historical midterm election result as Democrats took control of House and Senate.

In the immediate aftermath of the midterms, concerns about elevated AI valuations and heavy technology-sector spending triggered a sharp sell-off, particularly in semiconductor stocks.

Technology stocks rebounded on the last day of trade, but not enough to erase the week's losses. The major indices still ended the week in red. The S&P 500 was down around 3%, Nasdaq Composite declined 4% and Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1.7%.

In economy-related news, the October U.S. jobs report showed stronger-than-expected job growth, raising expectations of a Fed rate hike in December, adding another source of uncertainty for equities.

Amid a turbulent week for Wall Street, here were some of the stocks that caught the attention of investors:

Tesla and SpaceX dropped soon after the elections as Elon Musk's $500M bet on Republican campaigns proved unsuccessful. Both stocks rebounded somewhat on Friday but still ended in the red. Tesla was down 11.3% and SpaceX declined 2%. Musk also said on Friday that Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production in 2027 because of underwhelming sales.

AI and semiconductor stocks tumbled on Thursday as investors pulled back from technology stocks amid concerns over the outlook for data center spending following the U.S. midterm elections. The selloff came a day after Democrats secured a majority in Congress. Chipmakers bore the brunt of the declines. Advanced Micro Devices fell 17%, Intel lost 10.3%, Broadcom declined 10.4%, Nvidia dropped 9.2%, and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing fell 10.7%.

Marvell announced a definitive agreement to acquire Lumentum , an optical components manufacturer, in an all-stock transaction with an implied enterprise value of $115B. Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 shares of Marvell common stock for each Lumentum share they own. The acquisition is intended to strengthen Marvell's position in AI data center connectivity and optical technologies.

AppLovin shares surged more than 31% following its third-quarter earnings announcement. Revenue increased 55% year over year to $2.185B, while net income climbed 72% to $1.44B. The strong results were driven in part by improvements to its AI-powered advertising technology.

Qualcomm's shares fell nearly 10% on Thursday after its smartphone chip revenue tumbled 26% in the fourth quarter as rising memory prices weighed on handset demand. Overall, Qualcomm said it earned an adjusted $2.17 per share in the quarter as revenue fell 7% year-over-year to come in at $10.44B.

Apple reported fiscal fourth-quarter results that topped Wall Street's estimates. For the period ending Sept. 26, Apple said it earned $2.10 per share as revenue rose 12% year-over-year to come in at $114.48B. However, shares slipped as Apple forecast gross margins of 45%–46% for the December quarter, down from 47.9% in the September quarter. Following the report, CEO John Ternus warned that memory-chip prices were rising at an unprecedented rate.

Palantir Technologies shares fell even as the company reported strong third-quarter results and issued an upward revision to its full-year outlook, as investors focused on a slowdown in U.S. commercial bookings. U.S. commercial revenue surged 148% Y/Y to $984M in Q3, while U.S. government revenue jumped 96% to $953M.

Oracle priced a combined $20B stock and bond offering, including a $10B common stock sale at an 11.2% discount to its last closing price, as the company raises fresh capital amid its expanding AI infrastructure investments. The company priced 86.2M shares at $116 a piece, compared with its October 30 closing price of $130.67. The equity offering is expected to generate ~$9.9B in net proceeds. data.title: Paraguay's ex-President Peña faces prosecutors after impeachment, house arrest
data.description:
Paraguay’s former President Santiago Peña arrived at the Attorney General’s Office on Saturday to appear before prosecutors, a day after he was impeached and placed under house arrest amid a political and financial crisis triggered by the collapse of digital lender ueno.

Prosecutors said on Friday that charges against Peña were still being determined but could include influence peddling.

His removal brought Vice President Pedro Alliana to power, with the longtime ruling Colorado Party politician sworn in on Friday to complete Peña’s term through August 2028.

Lawmakers who backed Peña’s impeachment accused him of conflicts of interest, manipulating regulatory oversight and participating in an institutional cover-up involving the central bank.

Peña, who was a shareholder in ueno’s holding company until March 2025, has denied wrongdoing and said the bank’s problems were a regulatory matter.

The collapse has left millions of customers struggling to access their accounts and prompted protests in Asuncion. The scandal has also swept up senior officials and former ueno executives, while regulators have sought to reassure depositors and contain risks to the wider financial system.

data.title: E20 petrol supplied by PSU oil firms meets prescribed quality standards: Oil Min
data.description:
The government on Saturday defended the 20 per cent ethanol-blended petrol programme, saying tests of 893 samples collected across 27 states and Union Territories, including 56 in Karnataka, found them compliant with prescribed quality standards, as state-run oil companies challenged the Karnataka government's claims of excessive ethanol content in fuel sold at some retail outlets.

The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, in a statement, said Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL) had found ethanol content in all 893 samples within the prescribed 19-21 per cent range under the Bureau of Indian Standards' IS 17021 specification.

The 56 samples tested in Karnataka, covering different locations and all three oil marketing companies (OMCs), recorded ethanol content of 19-20 per cent, averaging 19.30 per cent, the ministry said.

The findings directly contradict a recent press release by Karnataka's Department of Food, Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs and Legal Metrology, which claimed that petrol samples collected from certain retail outlets in the state contained 26-31 per cent ethanol.

The three OMCs have questioned the sampling and testing procedures adopted in Karnataka's October 2026 exercise, arguing that the reported results cannot be independently validated without compliance with prescribed statutory procedures and disclosure of the technical details of the tests.

The dispute comes at a time when India's nationwide E20 programme, aimed at reducing dependence on imported crude oil and lowering emissions, has come under scrutiny over concerns about vehicle mileage, engine compatibility and the potential cost to consumers.

Under the Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel (Regulation of Supply, Distribution and Prevention of Malpractices) Order, 2005, read with the Marketing Discipline Guidelines (MDG) 2024, six one-litre samples must be drawn during an inspection. Two are handed to the dealer, two retained by the oil company or department, and two sent to an authorised laboratory.

The OMCs said samples collected during a September exercise were routed through the State Level Coordinator to designated company laboratories, but the subsequent October exercise was reportedly conducted without their representatives.

They said they had not received the corresponding retention samples, complete outlet-wise details or laboratory reports despite seeking them through the State Level Coordinator.

The companies also questioned certificates issued by a third-party laboratory, saying these did not specify the standard test method, dilution procedure or reference material used to determine ethanol content through Gas Chromatography.

Under IS 17021:2018, amended in August 2025, ethanol content must be determined through specified methods, including Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy, water extraction or Gas Chromatography under prescribed ASTM standards.

When Gas Chromatography is used, the standard requires samples to be diluted in a 1:1 ratio with oxygenate-free petrol and results corrected against an E10 certified reference material, the OMCs said.

The companies also flagged density readings of 0.742-0.749 grams per cubic centimetre in samples reportedly containing 26-31% ethanol, compared with 0.752-0.760 grams per cubic centimetre in their own E20 samples. Since ethanol is denser than petrol, a higher ethanol proportion would ordinarily be expected to increase the blend's density, they said.

The OMCs argued that the discrepancies reinforced the need for independent testing using prescribed methods and appropriate reference samples.

The government and OMCs also challenged estimates that E20 fuel could cause annual consumer mileage losses of around Rs 62,000 crore and vehicle repair costs of Rs 39,000 crore, taking the combined estimated burden to approximately Rs 1.01 lakh crore.

Citing studies involving the Inter-Ministerial Committee, Indian Oil, the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) and the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), the ministry said the mileage impact varied depending on vehicle category and engine calibration.

Vehicles calibrated for E20 could experience mileage reductions of around 1-2 per cent, while certain other vehicles could see declines of 3-6 per cent, according to the Petroleum Ministry's response to concerns over ethanol blending published on August 12, 2025.

The OMCs said applying a blanket assumption of 10% mileage loss across the entire vehicle population was not scientifically established. They also sought supporting vehicle-performance data, materials compatibility studies and documented repair costs for the Rs 39,000 crore repair estimate.

More than 30 crore two-wheelers and 4 crore four-wheelers have been running on E20 fuel for over three years, while more than 6 crore people visit petrol pumps daily, the companies said, arguing that there had been no reported widespread incidence of vehicle breakdowns attributable to fuel quality.

India's ethanol-blending programme, which began with a pilot initiative in 2001, has become a key component of the country's strategy to reduce its dependence on imported crude oil, support agricultural incomes and improve energy security.

According to Petroleum Ministry figures, the programme since the 2014-15 ethanol supply year has generated foreign exchange savings of more than Rs 1.97 lakh crore, substituted approximately 316 lakh metric tonnes of crude oil and reduced carbon dioxide emissions by around 952 lakh metric tonnes.

It has also resulted in payments of more than Rs 1.66 lakh crore to farmers.

During the 2025-26 ethanol supply year, which ended on October 31, 2026, the three public sector OMCs procured 1,089 crore litres of ethanol and blended 1,134 crore litres against petrol sales of approximately 5,673 crore litres, the ministry said.

The companies rejected suggestions that they had a commercial incentive to blend ethanol beyond prescribed levels, saying additional procurement would increase their costs.

The controversy has implications for the credibility of India's ethanol-blending programme, which has been scaled up rapidly as part of efforts to cut oil imports and emissions. While the government cites energy security, environmental and agricultural benefits, questions over fuel quality and vehicle performance could influence consumer confidence and the pace of wider acceptance of E20.

The three OMCs have asked the Karnataka government to share complete sampling documentation, outlet-wise laboratory reports and details of the testing methodology. They have also sought access to counterpart samples for independent testing at an authorised laboratory using the prescribed referee method, in the presence of state government and OMC representatives.

The companies said they were willing to participate in a joint sampling and testing exercise and that any deviation established through the prescribed procedure would be dealt with under applicable guidelines. PTI ANZ

data.title: Employers, watchmen at California ports extend contract talks
data.description:
The Los Angeles and Long Beach seaports employer group and the International Longshore and Warehouse Union Local 26 extended their bargaining deadline through November 20, averting a potential strike by about 2% of workers at the busiest US container port complex.

  • The Pacific Maritime Association said on Friday that additional talks were scheduled with the union representing about 250 maritime watchmen at the ports.

  • Local 26 did not immediately return a request for comment.

  • The union watchmen control and inspect truck and employee entries at terminal gates, provide terminal security and guard and track critical cargo crossing the docks.

  • A strike by the ILWU watchmen would disrupt operations at terminals that handle roughly 85% of the cargo at Long Beach and 33% at Los Angeles, PMA said.

  • The Los Angeles and Long Beach ports each reported all-time cargo volume records for September. Those shipments included retail goods for holiday sales, equipment for AI data center construction and auto parts.

data.title: Ex-FBI counterintelligence agent stole almost $2.5M in crypto
data.description:
A former FBI counterintelligence agent admitted to wire fraud and money laundering in stealing almost $2.5 million in cryptocurrency from unidentified adversarial nations and wallets that were under investigation.

Patrick Steven Yaroch, 37, used his investigative positions with access to FBI systems to steal cryptocurrency, then exchange and launder it through financial transactions to conceal its source and ownership.

Yaroch made about 100 fraudulent transfers related to 35 FBI investigations, gaining $2,474,380.66 in proceeds, according to a news release from the US Attorney’s Office, Eastern District of Virginia on Thursday.

He had earlier admitted to unauthorized transfers that involved about $1 million in digital assets, which was reported by Cointelegraph in August.

Yaroch paid off his debts and intended to use the proceeds to finance a new life in Portugal, where he planned to buy a vineyard, according to the statement.

The former agent admitted that his actions had compromised FBI investigations related to criminal groups and adversarial nations.

Yaroch faces up to 20 years in prison. His sentencing is set for March 4, 2027.

data.title: Fredun Pharmaceuticals Q2 results: Net profit jumps 90% on better demand
data.description:
Fredun Pharmaceuticals, a leading formulation manufacturer, reported that its net profit in the September quarter was up 90 per cent at ₹19 crore as compared to ₹10 crore in the same period last year on better demand.

Revenue was up 85 per cent at ₹266 crore (₹144 crore last year). EBITDA jumped 91 per cent to ₹43 crore (₹22 crore).

The company bought 26 per cent stake in Goodman Vetcare at a valuation of ₹300 crore in September. Goodman plans over 8 new stores and targets revenue of ₹100 crore by FY31.

In September 2026, Fredun acquired Furlicks from USV and its subsidiary Wellbeing Nutrition, marking its entry into pet wellness.

Furlicks makes easy-to-give oral strips covering skin and coat, gut health, joint care, calming, oral care and multivitamins.

The company plans to launch 16 new products over the next 6–9 months, taking the portfolio from 6 to 22 SKUs. The new launches will add formats such as cold-extruded, air-dried and freeze-dried products and functional biscuits.

Fredun launched a pet healthcare knowledge platform PAWTALKS with expert content on YouTube and Instagram.

Fredun Medhora, Managing Director, Fredun Pharmaceuticals, said the core formulations business was getting more efficient and added higher-margin while newer businesses in pet care, mobility, nutrition and dermaceuticals are now in a high-growth phase.

“These businesses carry better margins, so as they grow, they are steadily raising the quality of earnings. Fredun GX is now present in 19 states and pharmacies with distributors giving strong acceptance and repeat orders,” he said.

Pet care is one of the fastest-changing categories, as more pet parents treat their pets as family. The acquisition of stake in Goodman Vetcare and launch of PAWTALKS brings the company closer to a complete pet-wellness, he added.

“We are expanding capacity with the aim of building one of the largest manufacturing units at a single location in the country. We are also widening our product basket and strengthening the balance sheet,” he said.

data.title: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings files DRHP for IPO
data.description:
Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings Ltd (HCCH), the parent company of Coca-Cola’s India bottling arm, Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages, has filed draft papers with SEBI to raise funds through an initial public offering (IPO). The proposed IPO will be entirely an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 99.75 crore equity shares of face value ₹10 each by promoter Hindustan Coca-Cola Overseas Holdings Pte Ltd, according to the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP). The equity shares are proposed to be listed on BSE and NSE.

India is among the top five markets for the Coca-Cola Company in terms of unit case volume. In June, the company had said it was exploring a potential listing of HCCH. This move is in line with the beverage major’s global asset-light strategy. This also comes after it divested 40 per cent stake in the company to Jubilant Bhartia Group, which became one of the promoters of HCCH in July 2025.

Currently, Coca-Cola through Hindustan Coca-Cola Overseas Holdings Pte. Ltd., holds 60 per cent of HCCH, while Jubilant Beverages Limited holds 40 per cent.

HCCH, which operates through its material subsidiary HCCB, is the largest bottler within the Coca-Cola System in India based on units of concentrate sold. For the three month period ended June 30, the company’s retained units recorded revenue from operations of ₹4,310.17 crore, registering a year-on-year growth of 20.46 per cent., while total sales volume grew by 18.61 per cent. Its portfolio includes various brands including Thums Up, Coca-Cola, Maaza, Kinley, Minute Maid and Sprite among others. As of June 30, the Company owned, controlled and operated a network of 14 production facilities, supplemented by 8 co-pack units.

Kotak Mahindra Capital Company Limited, Citigroup Global Markets India Private Limited, J.P. Morgan India Private Limited, Morgan Stanley India Company Private Limited, Axis Capital Limited, Goldman Sachs (India) Securities Private Limited and IIFL Capital Services Limited are the Book Running Lead Managers to the IPO. KFin Technologies Limited is the registrar to the offer.

data.title: AvenuesAI Q2 profit climbs 6% to ₹72 crore on higher demand
data.description:
AvenuesAI Ltd (formerly known as Infibeam Avenues), a multinational financial technology and AI infrastructure company headquartered in GIFT City, reported a six per cent rise in net profit in the September quarter to ₹72 crore while revenue increased 47 per cent year-on-year to ₹2,879 crore, on the back of growing demand.

The company’s operating performance was supported by growth in its payments business and expansion across digital financial services, even as competition in the payments market put pressure on transaction margins.

For the first half of FY27, revenue from operations increased 71 per cent to ₹5,560 crore, while profit after tax grew 24 per cent to ₹156 crore. Operating EBITDA, excluding other income, stood at ₹199 crore, registering a 19 per cent year-on-year growth.

CCAvenue, the company’s flagship payment gateway business, continued to drive transaction volumes. Its payment processing value increased 19 per cent sequentially to around ₹1.77 lakh crore during the September quarter. However, the net take rate moderated to 5.06 basis points, reflecting pricing pressure and heightened competition in the payments industry.

Expansion plans

Vishwas Patel, Managing Director and CEO, AvenuesAI, said the company was focusing on expanding its offerings beyond payment processing to deepen relationships with merchants and enterprises.

The company is also integrating Rediff.com into its digital ecosystem, with RediffOne targeting enterprise communication and digital services and RediffPay focusing on consumer payments.

International expansion of CCAvenue, particularly in the US, UAE, Saudi Arabia and Australia, is another growth priority.

AvenuesAI is also developing TISco, its AI-led transaction intelligence platform, to offer solutions in fraud detection, risk assessment and merchant intelligence.

The company is seeking to evolve from a payments-led business into a broader AI-first fintech platform, with technology-led services expected to support revenue diversification and improve margins over the longer term.

data.title: Berkshire Hathaway's Quarterly Profit Falls After Investment Gains Shrink — WSJ
data.description:
By Krystal Hur

Berkshire Hathaway posted a 28% decline in quarterly net income after investment gains slumped and the conglomerate's insurance operations reported lower profits.

The Omaha, Neb.-based company continued to put more of its massive cash trove to work, repurchasing more of its own shares during the quarter.

Berkshire ended the third quarter with around $357 billion in cash and Treasury bills after accounting for a payable for purchasing some of the short-term government debt, a 2.1% decrease from three months earlier and the second-straight sequential drop.

The quarter also marked the end of Warren Buffett's long run as Berkshire's chairman. Buffett, 96, ceded the post to his son Howard Buffett in September. Greg Abel succeeded Buffett as CEO in January.

Net income fell to $22.11 billion, or $15,502 per Class A share, from $30.8 billion, or $21,413 a share, a year earlier.

The S&P 500 rose 2% during the third quarter, when U.S. Treasury yields surged.

Operating earnings, which exclude some investment results, slipped 5.8% to $12.71 billion from $13.49 billion. Profits from Berkshire's insurance-underwriting business fell sharply from a year ago, when the company benefited from a mild hurricane season and a turnaround from its auto insurer, Geico.

Berkshire's railroad and energy businesses reported higher profits, as did its portfolio of manufacturing, service and retailing companies.

Buffett has said that operating earnings are the better measure of the company's performance. Accounting rules require Berkshire to include unrealized gains and losses from its giant investment portfolio when it reports net income, meaning that short-term fluctuations in the stock market can cause big swings in quarterly income.

The company repurchased 4,536 Class A shares and 12,384,959 Class B shares during the third quarter, for around $9.6 billion.

Berkshire bought $2.4 billion of stocks during the September quarter and sold some $2.82.8 billion in the same period. Berkshire's largest holdings are Alphabet, American Express, Apple, Bank of America and Coca-Cola. The company is set to disclose more specifics on its stock portfolio in a regulatory filing later this month.

Berkshire's Class A shares are up more than 13% this year, and closed at a record high of around $869,301 on Wednesday.

The stock had previously been on a tumble after closing at a new high in May 2025, the day before Warren Buffett announced his retirement from the CEO post. But Berkshire rallied for much of October, as tech stocks began to slump amid fears over the AI build-out.
